Solution:
Equilibrium constant is highest in
CH₃-C(=O)-CH₂-C(=O)-H ⇌ CH₃-C(=OH)-CH=C(=O)-H

The equilibrium constant is highest because the enol form is stabilized by conjugation between the C=C double bond and the adjacent C=O group (α,β-unsaturated carbonyl system), and the product is also stabilized by hydrogen bonding between the OH group and the nearby carbonyl oxygen, making the forward reaction more favorable.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text:
In Cannizzaro type of reaction given below

[Diagram showing two benzaldehyde molecules reacting with OH⁻ to form benzyl alcohol and benzoate ion]

Which of the following is the slowest step?
options: Transfer of H⁺ ion to carbonyl carbon
Nucleophilic addition attack of ⁻OH at carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde
Transfer of hydride to the carbonyl group
Absorption of H⁺ ion to the medium
A.sol_text:
Answer: (3)
Solution:
Mechanism of Cannizzaro reaction
Experimentally the rate law has been determined for this reaction and has a third order or fourth order rate law depending on the aldehyde and the exact condition.

Rate = k[RCHO]²[OH⁻]
Rate = k[RCHO]²[OH⁻]²
To fit in the observed rate law the following mechanism has been proposed.
Step-1
OH⁻ + C(=O)-R-H ⇌ HO-C(-O⁻)-R-H

Step-2
HO-C(-O⁻)-R-H + OH⁻ ⇌ O⁻-C(-O⁻)-R-H (Dianion)

Step-3
O⁻-C(-O⁻)-R-H (Dianion) + C(=O)-R-H → [Slow (RDS)] → C(=O)-O⁻ + C-H₂-OH + R-H-H

Step-3 is slow step and rate determining step, where hydride transfer occurs.

Step-3 is slow step and rate determining step, where hydride transfer occurs.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The major product obtained in the reaction is
A.sol_text:
Step 1: Dilute OH⁻ with heat
The starting material has a ketone adjacent to a carboxylic acid derivative. Under dilute basic conditions with heat, a Knoevenagel-type condensation occurs, followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation forming a cyclopentanone ring fused to the cyclohexanone.

Step 2: CH₃MgBr with heat
The Grignard reagent attacks the carbonyl of the newly formed cyclopentanone ketone. After aqueous workup, this gives a secondary alcohol (hydroxyl group on the five-membered ring).

Step 3: O₂/Zn,H₂O oxidation
The secondary alcohol is oxidized to a ketone by the oxidizing conditions (O₂ with Zn,H₂O acting as a mild oxidant). Additionally, the double bond formed during the condensation may undergo oxidative cleavage or rearrangement.

The major product is obtained after all three transformations, yielding structure (1):
A bicyclic compound with a cyclohexanone (six-membered ring with ketone) fused to a cyclopentyl system bearing a carboxylic acid group (-CH(OH)COOH) at the bridgehead position.

Answer: (1)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match the following and choose the correct option
A.sol_text:
Solution:

For P: Starting material with CH₃ and OH groups on cyclohexane. Treatment with conc.H₂SO₄ causes dehydration to form a double bond (alkene). Then CH₃OH adds across the double bond via Markovnikov's rule to form product (4): cyclohexane with CH₃ and OCH₃ groups.

For Q: Starting material with CH₃ and OH groups. Treatment with 1. NaH converts OH to ONa⁻, then 2. CH₃I performs SN2 substitution to form product (3): cyclohexane with CH₃ and OCH₃ groups.

For R: Starting material with CH₃ and OH groups. Treatment with 1. HBr converts OH to Br, 2. Mg forms Grignard reagent (MgBr), and 3. CH₃I performs nucleophilic substitution to form product (2): cyclohexane with two CH₃ groups.

For S: Starting material with CH₃ and OH groups. Treatment with 1. Na converts OH to ONa⁺ with release of H₂, then 2. CH₃I performs SN2 substitution to form product (1): cyclohexane with CH₃ and OCH₃ groups.

Therefore: P → 4; Q → 3; R → 2; S → 1

A.sol_text:
sin x + cos y = √(y + 1/y)

y + 1/y ≥ 2 (∵ y > 0)
⇒ √(y + 1/y) ≥ √2

sin x + cos x = √2 sin(x + π/4) ≥ √2

Given equation has a solution only if
sin x + cos x = √2
⇒ x + π/4 = π/2
⇒ x = π/4

and √(y + 1/y) = √2 ⇒ y + 1/y = 2

⇒ (y - 1)² = 0 ⇒ y = 1

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If A and B are two non-zero n × n matrices such that A² + B = A²B, then
A.sol_text:
Given : A² + B = A²B ...(i)
⇒ A² + B − I = A²B − I
⇒ A²B − A² − B + I = I
⇒ A²(B − I) − I(B − I) = I
⇒ (A² − I)(B − I) = I
∴ A² − I is the inverse matrix of B − I and vice versa.
So, (B − I)(A² − I) = I
⇒ BA² − B − A² + I = I
∴ A² + B = BA² ...(ii)
So, by (i) and (ii)
A²B = BA²

A.sol_text:

tan[x²]π = 0

Solution:
If x∈[0, 1], tan[x²]π = tannπ, where [x²] = n∈ℤ = 0

∴ f(x) = {0/(ax²) + ax³ + b, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1; 2cos πx + tan⁻¹x, 1 < x ≤ 2}

⇒ f'(x) = {3ax², 0 < x < 1; -2π sin πx + 1/(1+x²), 1 < x < 2}

As the function is diff. in [0, 2]
⇒ Function is diff. at x = 1

∴ f'(1⁻) = f'(1⁺) ⇒ 3a = 1/2 ⇒ a = 1/6

Also f(x) will be continuous at x = 1

⇒ a + b = -2 + π/4

⇒ 1/6 + b = -2 + π/4

⇒ b = π/4 - 13/6

∴ a = 1/6 = 1/k₁ ⇒ k₁ = 6 (given) and b = π/4 - 26/12 = π/4 - 20/k₂ (given) ⇒ k₂ = 12

∴ ⌊(k₁² + k₂²)/20⌋ = ⌊(36 + 144)/20⌋ = ⌊180/20⌋ = 9

A.text: The number of ways in which all the letters of the word "EXTENSION" can be arranged such that no two E's and no two N's come together, is
A.sol_text:

Hint:
Use restricted permutation.

Solution:

(EE) X TNSION

×

A.text: If sin(2 cos⁻¹(cot(2 tan⁻¹ x))) = 0, x > 0, then which of the following is incorrect?
A.sol_text:
∴ sin(2 cos⁻¹(cot(2 tan⁻¹ x))) = 0, x > 0

A.text: The solution of the differential equation x²y²(x(dy/dx) + y) = a² is
A.sol_text:
We have
x²y²·(dy/dx) + xy³ = a²
or

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The number of circles that touch the line x − 3y − 4 = 0 at the point (1, −1) and also touch both the coordinate axes, is
A.sol_text:
The equation of circle touching the line x − 3y − 4 = 0 at the point (1, −1) is (x − 1)² + (y + 1)² + λ(x − 3y − 4) = 0

Solution:
The equation of circle touching the line x − 3y − 4 = 0 at the point (1, −1) is
(x − 1)² + (y + 1)² + λ(x − 3y − 4) = 0
⇒ x² + y² + x(λ − 2) + y(−3λ + 2) + 2 − 4λ = 0
whose centre is
C ≡ ((2 − λ)/2, (3λ − 2)/2)

From figure, (2 − λ)/2 > 0, (3λ − 2)/2 < 0 and
(2 − λ)/2 = (2 − 3λ)/2 ⇒ λ = 0
(if the circle touches both axes)
⇒ Circle is (x − 1)² + (y + 1)² = 0
Here, this circle does not touch the coordinate axes.
⇒ Number of required circles is zero.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A and B are two independent events. The probability that both A and B occur together is 1/6 and the probability that neither of them occurs is 1/3. The probability of occurrence of A is
A.sol_text:
P(A ∩ B) = 1/6 and P(A^c ∩ B^c) = 1/3

Now P(A ∪ B)^c = P(A^c ∩ B^c) = 1/3

⇒ 1 − P(A ∪ B) = 1/3 ⇒ P(A ∪ B) = 2/3

But P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

⇒ P(A) + P(B) = 5/6  ...... (i)

∴ A and B are independent events

∴ P(A ∩ B) = P(A) P(B) ⇒ P(A) P(B) = 1/6

[P(A) − P(B)]^2 = [P(A) + P(B)]^2 − 4P(A) P(B) = 25/36 − 4/6 = 1/36

⇒ P(A) − P(B) = ± 1/6  ...... (ii)

Solving (i) and (ii), we get P(A) = 1/2 or 1/3.

A.text: Tangents are drawn to the ellipse (x²/a²) + (y²/b²) = 1 (a > b) and the circle x² + y² = a² at the point where a common ordinate cut them (on the same side of the x-axis). Then the greatest acute angle between these tangents is given by
A.sol_text:
Tangent to the ellipse at P(a cos α, b sin α) is
(x/a)cos α + (y/b)sin α = 1 ...(i)
Tangent to the circle at Q(a cos α, a sin α) is
cos αx + sin αy = a ...(ii)
Now angle between tangents is θ,
Then tan θ = |(-b/a)cot α - (-cot α)|/|1 + (-b/a cot α)(-cot α)|
= |cot α(1 - b/a)|/|1 + (b/a)cot² α|
= |(a - b)/(a tan α + b cot α)|
= |(a - b)/(√a tan α - √b cot α)² + 2√(ab)|
(i) Now the greatest value of the above expression is
(a - b)/(2√(ab)) when √a tan α = √b cot α
(ii) ⇒ θ_maximum = tan⁻¹[(a - b)/(2√(ab))]

B.text: Let set A = {1001, 1002, 1003, …, 2500} and set B = {x : x is a natural number which is divisible by 3 or 5}, then the value of (1/100)n(A - B) is equal to
B.sol_text:
Answer : 8
Hint:
Use the principle of inclusion and exclusion
Solution:
∴ Number of divisors of 3 in set A = 500 = n(P)
Number of divisor of 5 in set A = 300 = n(Q)
Number of divisors of both 3 and 5 i.e. of 15 in set A = n(P ∩ Q) = 100
∴ n(B) = n(P ∪ Q) = n(P) + n(Q) − n(P ∩ Q)
= 500 + 300 − 100 = 700
∴ n(A − B) = 1500 − 700 = 800
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: Let f₁(x) and f₂(x) be even and odd functions respectively, where x²f₁(x) - 2f₁(1/x) = f₂(x), then the value of f₁(3) is
B.sol_text:
Answer: 0
Solution:
f₁(-x) = f₁(x) and f₂(-x) = -f₂(-x)
x²f₁(x) - 2f₁(1/x) = f₂(x) ... (i)
Replace x by -x,
x²f₁(-x) - 2f₁(-1/x) = f₂(-x)
⇒ x²f₁(x) - 2f₁(1/x) = -f₂(x) ...(ii)
From (i) and (ii), f₂(x) = 0
∴ x²f₁(x) = 2f₁(1/x)
Replace x by 1/x,
(1/x²)f₁(1/x) = 2f₁(x)
⇒ (x²/1)f₁(x) = 2x²f₁(x)
i.e. f₁(x) = 0

B.text: If P be a point on the parabola y² = 3(2x - 3) and M is the foot perpendicular drawn from P on the directrix of the parabola, then length of each side of an equilateral triangle SMP where S is focus of the parabola is ____.
B.sol_text:
y² = 6(x - 3/2)

Equation of directrix is x - 3/2 = -3/2 i.e., x = 0

Let coordinates of P be (3/2 + (3/2)t², 3t)

Therefore, coordinate of M are (0, 3t)

⇒ MS = √(9 + 9t²)

PS = 3/2 + (3/2)t²

∴ 9 + 9t² = (3/2 + (3/2)t²)² = (9/4)(1 + t²)²

4 = 1 + t²

∴ Length of side = 6
